newsitem.title: USA: Oxford shares drop despite strong Q4.
newsitem.headline: Oxford shares drop despite strong Q4.

text.p: Shares of Oxford Health Plans Inc dropped 2-1/2 to 59 on Tuesday despite a strong fourth quarter earnings report.
"They had sterling enrollment growth. Strong earnings. Stellar numbers overall," said Merrill Lynch analyst Margo Vignola. "They're off on some basic profit taking."
Earlier on Tuesday, Oxford posted fourth quarter earnings of $0.39 per diluted share on revenues of $880.3 million, compared to $0.21 per diluted share on revenues of $537.4 million last year.
"Oxford has a very good quarter. Operations are strong," said Gary Frazier, an analyst with Bear Stearns.
Frazier said Oxford Health's earnings and enrollment growth exceeded expectations and the medical loss ratio matched analysts' estimates.
Oxford's 64 percent revenue growth fell slightly short of some Wall Street estimates of 68 percent, Frazier said.
Oxford's results also included some costs related to converting to a new computer system.
"There may be concerns about the computer costs and revenue growth, but these concerns may be a little overblown. Revenue growth of 64 percent is still very exceptional," Frazier said.
Shares of health maintenance organization companies rallied last week after comments from United Healthcare Corp, the nation's largest HMO company, were taken positively by the market.
On Tuesday, United Healthcare lost 1-5/8 to 52-3/4, Aetna Inc fell 1-1/4 to 85-1/4 and PacifiCare dropped 11/16 to 83-1/16.
